page.overview:
Who is Indominus rex's sibling?

A second sibling Indominus rex was cloned by Dr. Henry Wu for Jurassic World. However, prior to her debut, she was killed and cannibalized by her sister. Neither Indominus is known to have been given any form of name or designation, and were most likely identified solely by specimen numbers. As only one survived, distinguishing between the two is not necessary in most cases.

Both Indominus hatched within the same day at some point after 2012 on Isla Nublar. This followed roughly three years of experimentation after their creation was authorized on April 4, 2012 by Masrani Global Corporation CEO Simon Masrani. The species development took place in the Hammond Creation Laboratory. After hatching, each one was fitted with a subdermal RFID tracking implant which would constantly update the Jurassic World computer network with the dinosaurs’ locations and biometrics. The implants were placed in the animals’ backs, just above the left shoulder in at least one of them. The Indominus were intended to live in a paddock with physical walls and therefore would not have been affected by the park’s invisible fencing system, but unlike other animals where this was the case, the Indominus tracking implants were programmed to shock them if they came too close to other park attractions. This was presumably an additional security measure. At an unknown point prior to November 2015, one of the Indominus cannibalized the other. This information was not relayed to Simon Masrani, who had not yet seen the animals in person.

The Indominus rex hatched out of her egg, alongside her sibling.
